title: Without holiness no one will see the Lord
source_text: VIII. Ac profecto qui pertenderent in fidelibus nulla opera vere bona justa & sancta reperiri, hoc ipso illos salute excluderent, & aeternis inferni ignibus adjudicarent. Nam sine sanctificatione nemo videbit Dominum. Et [marg.: Mat. c. 5.] nisi inquit Christus, abundaverit justitia vestra plusquam scribarum & Pharisaeorum, non intrabitis in regnum coelorum. Quinimo declarat Dominus arborem omnem quae non fert fructum bonum excindendam esse & in ignem mittendam, Matth. cap. 7. Item palmitem omnem, qui fructum in eo non fert, tollendum esse atque colligendum, ut in ignem mittatur, & ardeat, Joh. 15.
pass_a_gloss: VIII. And indeed those who would maintain that no truly good just & holy works are found in the faithful, would by this very thing exclude them from salvation, & sentence them to the eternal fires of hell. For without sanctification no one will see the Lord. And [marg.: Mat. c. 5.] unless says Christ, your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes & Pharisees, you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven. Nay rather the Lord declares that every tree which does not bear good fruit is to be cut down & cast into the fire, Matth. chap. 7. Likewise that every branch, which does not bear fruit in him, is to be taken away & gathered, that it may be cast into the fire, & burn, John 15.
pass_b_english: Thesis VIII. In fact anyone who insisted that believers have no truly good, just and holy works would by that very claim shut them out of salvation and condemn them to the eternal fire of hell.

Without holiness no one will see the Lord. Christ says, 'Unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will not enter the kingdom of heaven' (Matthew 5). The Lord even declares that every tree that does not bear good fruit is to be cut down and thrown into the fire (Matthew 7), and that every branch in him that bears no fruit is to be taken away and gathered up to be thrown into the fire and burned (John 15).

choices.why: Le Blanc's thesis: the works of the regenerate are truly, not just apparently, good, even though they are not perfect.
